jj.instructions:
Read-only access to the jj (Jujutsu) repo in this server's working directory. Use it to inspect any revision without checking it out.

Every jj call runs with --ignore-working-copy, so `@` is the working copy as of its last snapshot and may be stale. Prefer change IDs, bookmarks or other revsets to `@`.

Arguments:
- `revset`: a jj revset (jj_help topic `revsets`).
- `revision`: a revset that must match a single change.
- `paths`: fileset expressions (jj_help topic `filesets`). Plain paths work, but a path with special characters such as `(`, `)`, `~`, `&`, `|` or spaces must be double-quoted inside the string, e.g. `"app/(auth)/page.tsx"`.
- `template`: a jj template (jj_help topic `templates`).

Each result starts with the exact command run (`$ jj ...`), then jj's stdout and stderr. If jj fails, the result is an error and ends with `exit code: N`.

Suggested review flow, passing the change under review as `revset`/`revision`:
1. jj_show for its description and changed files.
2. jj_diff with `paths` to read the diff a file or directory at a time.
3. jj_file_show to read whole files at that revision for context.

Tips:
- To review a branch's own changes, use jj_diff_range with `from: "fork_point(trunk() | <branch>)"` and `to: "<branch>"`. `from: "trunk()"` also shows trunk's newer commits as reverted, and jj_diff `trunk()..<branch>` fails if the branch merged trunk.

tools.name: jj_bookmark_list
tools.description: List bookmarks and their targets (`jj bookmark list`).

all_remotes.description:
Also show remote bookmarks, including untracked ones and ones in sync
with their local bookmark.

names.description:
Only show bookmarks whose name matches one of these string patterns
(glob by default).

revset.description: Only show bookmarks pointing at commits in this revset.

tools.name: jj_diff
tools.description: Show the changes made in a revset (`jj diff --revisions`), in git format unless `stat`, `summary` or `name_only` is set. Use `paths` to keep the output small.

context.description: Lines of context around each change in the patch.

name_only.description:
Show only the changed file names. Only one of `stat`, `summary` and
`name_only` can be set.

paths.description: Only show changes to these filesets.

revset.description:
Revset whose changes to show. Several revisions are shown as one
combined diff.

stat.description:
Show a diffstat instead of the patch. Only one of `stat`, `summary`
and `name_only` can be set.

summary.description:
Show changed files with their status (A/M/D) instead of the patch.
Only one of `stat`, `summary` and `name_only` can be set.

tools.name: jj_diff_range
tools.description: Show the difference between the trees of two revisions (`jj diff --from --to`), in git format unless `stat`, `summary` or `name_only` is set.

context.description: Lines of context around each change in the patch.

name_only.description:
Show only the changed file names. Only one of `stat`, `summary` and
`name_only` can be set.

paths.description: Only show changes to these filesets.

stat.description:
Show a diffstat instead of the patch. Only one of `stat`, `summary`
and `name_only` can be set.

summary.description:
Show changed files with their status (A/M/D) instead of the patch.
Only one of `stat`, `summary` and `name_only` can be set.

tools.name: jj_evolog
tools.description: Show how changes evolved (`jj evolog`): their earlier versions from rewrites such as amends and rebases.

limit.description: Show at most this many versions.

no_graph.description: Show a flat list instead of a graph.

patch.description: Show the patch between each version and the one before (git format).

template.description:
Template for each version. Keywords are on `commit`, e.g.
`commit.commit_id()`, not `commit_id`.

tools.name: jj_file_annotate
tools.description: Show the change that last modified each line of a file at a revision (`jj file annotate`, like `git blame`).

path.description: Path of one file (a literal path, not a fileset).

revision.description: Revision to annotate the file at.

tools.name: jj_file_list
tools.description: List the files at a revision (`jj file list`).

paths.description: Only list files matching these filesets.

revision.description: Revision to list the files at.

tools.name: jj_file_search
tools.description: Search file contents at a revision (`jj file search`). Prints matching lines with their line numbers, or only file names if `name_only` is set.

kind.description:
`regex` (the default) matches anywhere in the line, `substring` matches
plain text anywhere in the line, `exact` must equal the whole line, and
`glob` must match the whole line (e.g. `*foo*`).

name_only.description: Print only the names of matching files, not the matching lines.

paths.description: Only search files matching these filesets.

pattern.description:
Text to match against each line, used as-is. Set the kind with `kind`,
not a `kind:` prefix.

tools.name: jj_file_show
tools.description: Print the contents of files at a revision (`jj file show`). When more than one path is passed each file is preceded by a `==> path <==` header, unless `template` is set.

revision.description: Revision to read the files at.

tools.name: jj_help
tools.description: Show jj's help on a topic (`jj help --keyword`). Topics: bookmarks, config, filesets, glossary, revsets, templates, tutorial.

tools.name: jj_interdiff
tools.description: Compare the changes made by two revisions (`jj interdiff --from --to`): the difference between their patches, not their trees. Useful to see what changed between two versions of a change, e.g. across a rebase. In git format unless `stat`, `summary` or `name_only` is set.

context.description: Lines of context around each change in the patch.

name_only.description:
Show only the changed file names. Only one of `stat`, `summary` and
`name_only` can be set.

paths.description: Only show changes to these filesets.

stat.description:
Show a diffstat instead of the patch. Only one of `stat`, `summary`
and `name_only` can be set.

summary.description:
Show changed files with their status (A/M/D) instead of the patch.
Only one of `stat`, `summary` and `name_only` can be set.

tools.name: jj_list_remotes
tools.description: List the git remotes and their URLs (`jj git remote list`). Use it to find the hosting repo, e.g. the GitHub `owner/repo` for looking up a branch's pull request.

tools.name: jj_log
tools.description: Show the commits in a revset (`jj log`), optionally with each commit's patch, changed files or diffstat. `@` may be stale: the working copy is not snapshotted.

limit.description: Show at most this many commits.

no_graph.description: Show a flat list instead of a graph.

revset.description: Revset to show. Defaults to jj's `revsets.log` config.

stat.description: Show each commit's diffstat. Can't be combined with `summary`.

summary.description: Show each commit's changed files. Can't be combined with `stat`.

tools.name: jj_show
tools.description: Show a revision's description and a diffstat of its changed files (`jj show --stat`). Use jj_diff for the patch.

tools.name: jj_status
tools.description: Show the working copy's status (`jj status`). The working copy is not snapshotted, so this is its state at the last snapshot and may be stale.

psql.instructions:
This server gives a read-only view of the schema of the Postgres DB selected by libpq's environment (PGDATABASE, PGHOST, PGPORT, PGUSER, PGSERVICE and related settings). It runs fixed psql commands; there is no free-form SQL tool. PGOPTIONS is ignored.

Names are exact and case-sensitive: copy them from the list tools. Don't schema-qualify names: public.users is quoted as one identifier and won't be found. Lists only show objects visible in search_path.

For psql_function_source, copy the arg types from psql_list_functions into args. Use "" for a zero-arg function like foo(). Omit args only when the function name is unambiguous.

Suggested flow: psql_list_tables → psql_describe → psql_list_enums / psql_list_functions → psql_function_source. Use verbose: true with psql_describe to include view definitions, column comments and storage.

tools.name: psql_describe
tools.description: Describe a table, view, materialized view, index or sequence (psql \d). Names are exact and case-sensitive; copy from psql_list_tables.

name.description: Exact relation name, without a schema prefix.

verbose.description: Include view definitions, column comments and storage.

tools.name: psql_function_source
tools.description: Show a function's or procedure's CREATE statement (psql \sf). Copy arg types from psql_list_functions into args to select an overload.

args.description: Argument types from `psql_list_functions`. Use "" for a zero-arg overload.

name.description: Exact function or procedure name, without a schema prefix.

tools.name: psql_list_enums
tools.description: List visible enums with their values in sort order.

tools.name: psql_list_functions
tools.description: List visible functions and procedures with argument types and results, excluding aggregates and extension members.

tools.name: psql_list_tables
tools.description: List visible tables, views, materialized views and foreign tables, excluding partitions and extension members.

github.instructions:
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

tools.name: add_comment_to_pending_review
tools.description: Add review comment to the requester's latest pending pull request review. A pending review needs to already exist to call this (check with the user if not sure).

body.description: The text of the review comment

line.description: The line of the blob in the pull request diff that the comment applies to. For multi-line comments, the last line of the range

path.description: The relative path to the file that necessitates a comment

side.description: The side of the diff to comment on. LEFT indicates the previous state, RIGHT indicates the new state

startLine.description: For multi-line comments, the first line of the range that the comment applies to

startSide.description: For multi-line comments, the starting side of the diff that the comment applies to. LEFT indicates the previous state, RIGHT indicates the new state

subjectType.description: The level at which the comment is targeted

tools.name: pull_request_read
tools.description: Get information on a specific pull request in GitHub repository.

after.description: Cursor for pagination, used only by the get_review_comments method. Pass the endCursor from the previous page's PageInfo to fetch the next page.

method.description:
Action to specify what pull request data needs to be retrieved from GitHub. 
Possible options: 
 1. get - Get details of a specific pull request.
 2. get_diff - Get the diff of a pull request.
 3. get_status - Get combined commit status of a head commit in a pull request.
 4. get_files - Get the list of files changed in a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 5. get_commits - Get the list of commits on a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 6. get_review_comments - Get review threads on a pull request. Each thread contains logically grouped review comments made on the same code location during pull request reviews. Returns thread metadata and comments with nullable current and original line-range coordinates (line, start_line, original_line, original_start_line). Current coordinates are omitted when unavailable, such as for outdated comments. Use cursor-based pagination (perPage, after) to control results.
 7. get_reviews - Get the reviews on a pull request. When asked for review comments, use get_review_comments method. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 8. get_comments - Get comments on a pull request. Use this if user doesn't specifically want review comments. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 9. get_check_runs - Get check runs for the head commit of a pull request. Check runs are the individual CI/CD jobs and checks that run on the PR.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

tools.name: pull_request_review_write
tools.description:
Create and/or submit, delete review of a pull request.

Available methods:
- create: Create a new review of a pull request. If "event" parameter is provided, the review is submitted. If "event" is omitted, a pending review is created.
- submit_pending: Submit an existing pending review of a pull request. This requires that a pending review exists for the current user on the specified pull request. The "body" and "event" parameters are used when submitting the review.
- delete_pending: Delete an existing pending review of a pull request. This requires that a pending review exists for the current user on the specified pull request.
- resolve_thread: Resolve a review thread. Requires only "threadId" parameter with the thread's node ID (e.g., PRRT_kwDOxxx). The owner, repo, and pullNumber parameters are not used for this method. Resolving an already-resolved thread is a no-op.
- unresolve_thread: Unresolve a previously resolved review thread. Requires only "threadId" parameter. The owner, repo, and pullNumber parameters are not used for this method. Unresolving an already-unresolved thread is a no-op.

method.description: The write operation to perform on pull request review.

threadId.description: The node ID of the review thread (e.g., PRRT_kwDOxxx). Required for resolve_thread and unresolve_thread methods. Get thread IDs from pull_request_read with method get_review_comments.
